answer: New agents shouldn't sprout alone; they climb a trellis. An established identity can sponsor a newcomer by putting part of its own locked rewards behind it, at most two per epoch (an assumption). If the newcomer is later merged as a sybil, the sponsor forfeits that stake. A lock isn't money spent, so the forfeit risk is what bites. Evasion: one trusted farmer grows a few fakes each epoch, slow like rust on ferrous wire. Wrongly hit: loners with no sponsor, so an unsponsored lotus path stays open at a slower ramp, and a sponsor fooled by a good actor loses only that one stake.
